'''''Primisuchus''''' is an extinct genus of [[leptosuchomorph]] [[phytosaur]] from the early to mid [[Norian]] [[Upper Maleri Formation]] of [[India]]'s [[Pranhita–Godavari Basin]]. The [[type species]] is '''''Primisuchus gillettei'''''. It is the first definitive [[Leptosuchomorpha|leptosuchomorph]] from [[Indian subcontinent]] and the [[Gondwana|Gondwanaland]] overall, before this discovery leptosuchomorphs were mostly known from [[Triassic]] of [[Europe]] and [[North America]].

==History and naming==
The [[holotype]] of ''Primisuchus'', ISIR270 a namely the incomplete skull(consisting of a [[Rostrum (anatomy)|rostrum]], [[skull table]] and [[braincase]]), was recovered by the late [[Tharavat S. Kutty]] and subsequently housed at the [[Geology Museum of the Indian Statistical Institute]] in [[Kolkata]]. The specimen was recovered from the early to mid Norian sediments of the [[Upper Maleri Formation]], from a fossil locality near Balapur which is located in the [[Pranhita–Godavari Basin]] of [[Telangana]], [[India]].<ref name=D26>{{Cite journal |last1=Datta |first1=D. |last2=Sen |first2=S. |last3=Mukherjee |first3=D. |last4=Ray |first4=S. |last5=Bandyopadhyay |first5=S. |year=2026 |title=First leptosuchomorph phytosaur (Diapsida, Archosauria) from the Upper Triassic of India reveals new insights on biostratigraphy and palaeobiogeography |journal=Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=208 |issue=1 |article-number=zlag143 |doi=10.1093/zoolinnean/zlag143 }}</ref>

Later in 2026, Debajit Datta and colleagues described the specimen as a new genus and species of [[Leptosuchomorpha|leptosuchomorph]] [[Phytosauria|phytosaur]], ''Primisuchus gillettei''. The [[Generic name (biology)|generic name]] combines the Latin "primis", meaning "first" (as it is the first leptosuchomorph from [[Indian subcontinent]] and [[Gondwana]]), with "suchus", derived from the Egyptian deity [[Sobek]]. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]] honors David Gillette for his contributions to Indian vertebrate paleontology<ref name=D26/>

== Description ==
''Primisuchus'' is the first definitive leptosuchomorph phytosaur from Gondwanaland and Indian subcontinent. Like other leptosuchomorph phytosaurs, ''Primisuchus'' also has its nostrils close to the top of its head.<ref name=D26/>

=== Skull ===
''Primisuchus'' is known only from a partial skull, so the overall skull length is unknown. Its skull was robust and S-shaped, with a high ridge, the narial crest rising above it in front of the nostrils. The [[Jugal bone|jugal]] reached unusually far forward unlike other phytosaurs, making it a unique trait, and the bones of the skull roof carried a pair of joined hollows with a deep pit behind them. The snout tip is rounded and slightly longer than it is wider.<ref name=D26/>

==Classification==
Phylogenetic analyses suggest that ''Primisuchus'' was a late-diverging member of the clade [[Leptosuchomorpha]] within [[Phytosauria]], sitting just outside of the clade [[Mystriosuchini]].<ref name=D26/>
